Confirmed: `Segment.get()` (an unlocked read path) calls `recordRead(entry, now)`, which appends the entry to the per-segment `recencyQueue` (a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`) without acquiring the segment lock. That queue is later drained — under the segment lock (`@GuardedBy("this")`) — by `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()`, which replays the recorded accesses into the LRU `accessQueue` (`guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java:2542-2547` and `:2590-2602`).

ANSWER: On a read, `Segment.get()` calls `recordRead(entry, now)` (LocalCache.java), which adds the entry to the Segment's unlocked `recencyQueue` (a ConcurrentLinkedQueue) instead of touching the LRU list directly; `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()` later runs under the segment lock to replay those entries into the `accessQueue` and fix up LRU order.
